CITY OF AVALON PLANNING COMMISSION AGENDA
  City Hall Council Chambers ∙ 410 Avalon Canyon Road, Avalon, CA
  Regular Meeting – June 18, 2025 at 5:00 p.m.

  This meeting is viewable in person at the Council Chambers or via livestream:

  Facebook: (http://www.facebook.com/CityOfAvalonOfficial)
  YouTube (http://www.youtube.com/cityofavalonca)
  Website (http://www.cityofavalon.com/meetings)
  Cable (Catalina Broadband Solutions Channel 3)

  The Council Chambers can accommodate a maximum of 30 participants, at which point
  the general public may address the Planning Commission on an agenda item by waiting
  in the City Hall Courtyard and entering the Chambers one at a time. No one will be
  admitted into the Council Chambers who is ill or exhibiting symptoms of COVID-19. The
  Planning Commission is not accepting live comments electronically at this time.

  The public can submit written comments prior to 12:00 p.m. 3 days prior to the meeting
  in person to the Planning Department at City Hall or via email to
  dromo@cityofavalon.gov
  .

  Staff reports for each agenda item are posted a minimum of 72 hours prior to the
  meeting and are available for review in person or on the City website at cityofavalon.

  In compliance with the Americans with Disability Act, if you need special assistance to participate
  in this meeting, please contact Gabrielle Morones, City Clerk’s office (310) 510-0220 ext. 119.
  Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements
  to ensure accessibility to this meeting. (28 CFR 35. 102-35.104 ADA Title II). All public records
  relating to an agenda item on this agenda are available for the public inspection at the time the
  records are distributed to all, or a majority of all, members of the Planning Commission. Such
  records shall be available at City Hall located at 410 Avalon Canyon Road.

  CALL TO ORDER

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE/ROLL CALL

  ORAL COMMUNICATION: This is the time for any member of the public to address the
  Planning Commission on any matter not on the agenda that is within the subject matter
  jurisdiction of the City. The Brown Act, with limited exceptions, does not allow the
  Commission or staff to discuss or take action on issues brought forth under Public
  Comment. Concerns may be referred to staff or placed on the next available agenda.
  Please note that comments from the public will also be taken on each agenda item.
  Comments shall be limited to three minutes per person.

   AVALON PLANNING COMMISSION
  STAFF REPORT – PC# 2878
  Wednesday, May 21, 2025

  Application File: VAR, SPR
Item No.  3 – Public Hearing  Submitted by: Kelly Ribuffo, Contract Planner

Pursuant to approved motion of the Planning Commission during the public hearing on April 16,
2025, approve a Variance and Site Plan to allow demolition of an existing single-family residence
and construction of a new two-story single-family residence in the Multiple Residential, High
Density (HD) zone. The Proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15303 (New Construction or
Conversion of Small Structures). The proposed project is located within the Coastal Zone and is
excluded from Coastal Development Permit requirements per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC)
Section 9-8.102.b.7.

  Applicant/Owner: Eric Simison
  Files:  VAR, SPR
  Location of Project: 306 Claressa Avenue
  APN:  7480-037-003
  PC #:  2878
  General Plan:  High Density Residential
  Zone:  Multiple Family, High Density (HD)

  BACKGROUND

At the April 16, 2025 regular meeting, the Planning Commission voted 5-0 to approve the request
for a Variance and Site Plan for the proposed project at 306 Sumner Avenue. Based on the direction
provided by the Planning Commission with the motion, staff has prepared a new draft resolution
for approval of the project as presented by the applicant, including standard conditions of approval
to ensure compliance with applicable permitting regulations.

  ATTACHMENTS

  1. Draft Resolution No. PC 25-07
  2. April 16, 2025 Planning Commission Staff Report and Attachments (under separate cover)

  1
   RESOLUTION NO. PC 25-07

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  AVALON, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A VARIANCE AND SITE PLAN
  FOR CONSTRUCTION OF A NEW SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENCE IN
  THE DESIGNATED AREA OF THE MULTIPLE RESIDENTIAL, HIGH
  DENSITY ZONE, LOCATED AT 306 CLARESSA AVENUE, AVALON,
  CALIFORNIA

  WHEREAS, Eric J. Simison (“Applicant”) filed an application (“Application”) for a
Variance and Site Plan (PC#2878) to approve the demolition of an existing single-family residence
and construction of a new two-story single-family residence with a variance for the rear setback
(“Project”) on the property located at 306 Claressa Avenue, APN 7480-037-003 (“Site”); and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission has authority per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC)
Sections 9-8.401 and 9-8.203.a to review and take action on the subject applications for a Variance
and a Site Plan; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is categorized High Density Residential by the General Plan Land
Use Element and is located within the designated area of the Multiple Family, High Density (HD)
zoning district as defined by AMC Section 9-5.406; and

  WHEREAS, the Site is located within the Coastal Zone and is excluded from Coastal
Development Permit requirements per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-8.102.b.7; and

  WHEREAS, the Project was found to be categorically exempt from CEQA per State
CEQA Guidelines 15303 (Class 3 – New Construction or Conversion of Small Structures). No
public review is required; and
  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission conducted one duly advertised public hearing on
April 16, 2025, at which time interested persons had an opportunity to testify either in support of
or opposition to granting a Variance and Site Plan upon property described in attached Exhibit
“A”; and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites for the consideration of the Variance and Site
Plan have occurred.

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED that the Planning Commission of the City of
Avalon does hereby approve a Variance and Site Plan for the demolition of an existing single-
family residence and construction of a new two-story single-family residence with a variance for
the rear setback located at 306 Claressa Avenue, based on the following findings:

  1
 SECTION 1 – ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed Project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15303 (Class 3 – New Construction or
Conversion of Small Structures) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment.

The Class 3 exemption includes the construction and location of limited numbers of small new
facilities or structures. The Project involves demolition of an existing single-family residence and
construction of a new single-family building in an urbanized area of the city. As such, the Project
is not expected to have a detrimental impact on the environment of the project site or surrounding
area.

Furthermore, none of the exceptions to the use of categorical exemptions stated in State CEQA
Guidelines section 15300.2 apply: The Project is not located in a particularly sensitive environment
because it is proposed in an area already developed for residential uses. No cumulative impact
would occur from this Project’s approval because only a single application has been submitted and
no future development is proposed at this time. There will be no significant effect on the
environment because the Project is only for a single-family residence that would have only minor
impacts. No damage to scenic resources will occur because this Project will replace an existing
structure and is consistent with adopted development standards. The Project is not located on a
hazardous waste site, and the Project does not involve a historical resource.

SECTION 2 – FINDINGS

Annual Growth Policy:

The growth policy provides that new commercial development would only be permitted with
confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate fresh water is
available. The Project involves permitting of a new residential building, which requires evaluation
of an allocation for water service. Water demand for residential buildings is calculated based on
the number of bedrooms in the unit. The existing residence is two bedrooms, and the proposed
residence is also two bedrooms. Since the number of bedrooms remains the same, no water
allocation is required for the construction of the Project as proposed, as there is no increase in
water demand. Therefore, staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that
the proposed project is in compliance with the 2025 Annual Growth Policy.

Affordable Housing Ordinance:

This ordinance is not applicable to the proposed Project since the proposal does not include the
development of five or more residential units.

Variance:

The proposed Project must be granted a Variance for height per AMC Section 9-6.204.d.1. AMC
Section 9-8.405 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Variance as follows:

  2
 1. Variances from the terms of the Zoning Ordinance shall be granted only when,
  because of special circumstances applicable to the property including size, shape,
  topography, location or surroundings, the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance
  deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and
  under identical zoning classification.

  The urban fabric of Avalon is relatively compact, with approximately 80-90 acres of
  existing development already located within the valley floor and the immediately
  surrounding hillsides. Individually owned lots in Avalon comprise less than 1% of the total
  city acreage. Therefore, it is important to maximize the use of land within the city within
  the development parameters of each zoning district, so long as it is consistent with overall
  community character.

  The historic development pattern of “the Flats” is dense, with small, narrow lots which
  have varying and sometimes zero setbacks between properties. Such development is seen
  along the east side of Claressa Avenue, where the subject property is located in the
  “designated area” of the HD zone.

  The Applicant has requested a variance for a rear setback of 0 feet, where a 1-foot setback
  is required pursuant to AMC Section 9-5.406.

  It is the opinion of the Planning Commission that strict application of the setbacks as
  written in AMC Section 9-5.406 would deprive the subject property of the same privileges
  enjoyed by other properties along Claressa Avenue, which are predominantly developed
  with 0-foot setbacks. Furthermore, lack of access to the alley between Claressa Avenue
  and Clemente Avenue due to unpermitted private development constitutes a special
  circumstance that restricts access to and the development potential of the property.
  Approving the setback variance would allow the property owner to develop the lot to same
  size as other properties on the street and also be consistent with the established
  development pattern of the neighborhood.

  Therefore, the proposed variances may be granted in conformance with the findings of the
  municipal code, as the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance would deprive the subject
  property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and under identical zoning
  classification.

2. Any variance granted shall be subject to such conditions as will assure that the
  adjustment thereby authorized shall not constitute a grant of special privileges
  inconsistent with the limitations upon other properties in the vicinity and zone in
  which such property is situated.

  It is the opinion of the Planning Commission that strict application of the setbacks as
  written in AMC Section 9-5.406 would deprive the subject property of the same privileges
  enjoyed by other properties along Claressa Avenue, which are predominantly developed
  with 0-foot setbacks. Standard conditions of approval are included in this resolution to

  3
   ensure the project complies with all building and safety regulations for construction of the
  proposed project.

  Therefore, granting of the requested variances does not constitute granting of special
  privileges as the variance allows development of the property within the parameters
  intended for the “designated area” of the HD zone.

  3. A variance shall not be granted for a parcel of property which authorizes a use or
  activity which is not otherwise expressly authorized by the zone regulation governing
  the parcel of property.

  Single-family dwelling units are permitted by right within the HD zone. The application does
  not include a request for any use that is not permitted within the zoning district.

  4. No variances shall be granted which reduce or adversely affect access to or along the
  shoreline, including physical or visual qualities of access.

  The project site is located over 930 feet from the mean high tide line of Avalon Bay. The site
  is not adjacent to, nor provides direct or indirect visual or physical access to, the shoreline of
  Avalon Bay, coastal hillsides or bluffs, or other significant viewsheds identified in the Avalon
  Local Coastal Plan.

  5.  The variance shall be consistent with the Local Coastal Program.

  The proposed project implements the following General Plan Policies:

  Policy II-9 of the Land Use Element:

  “Encourage infill of the City Center area and where appropriate, increase the intensity of
  development on vacant and underutilized properties, in lieu of expanded development
  outward into Avalon’s hillsides, natural areas and open space.”

  The project proposes to demolish an existing single-family residence and construct a new,
  larger single-family residence in its place. Individually owned lots in Avalon comprise less
  than 1% of the total city acreage. Therefore, it is important to maximize the use of land
  within the city within the development parameters of each zoning district, so long as it is
  consistent with overall community character. The project is designed to maximize the
  density of development on the property in the urbanized center of Avalon consistent with
  the historic development pattern of the neighborhood. Infill construction on the existing lot
  does not contribute to outward expansion into the surrounding natural areas or open spaces
  at the perimeter of the city.

Site Plan Review:

The proposed Project requires approval of a Site Plan per AMC Section 9-8.201. AMC Section 9-
8.203 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Site Plan Review as follows:

  4
 1. Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall take
  place in compliance with all applicable provisions of this title. (AMC Section 9-
  8.203.a)

  With the requested variance for tthe rear setback, the proposed project complies with all
  development standards as set forth in AMC for development on the project site in the
  Multiple Residential, High Density (HD) zone as discussed in Variance Findings #1
  thought 5.

2. Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall be
  considered on the basis of the suitability of the site for the particular use or
  development intended, and the total development, including the application of
  prescribed development standards, shall be so arranged as to avoid traffic congestion,
  insure the protection of public health, safety and general welfare, prevent adverse
  effects on neighboring property and shall be in general accord with all elements of the
  General Plan. (AMC Section 9-8.203.b)

  The proposed project is designed to fit within the density, scale, and mass of existing
  development along Claressa Avenue. This area is located in the “Flats”, which has a
  predominantly flat topography. Existing residential development varies between one- and
  two-stories in height. With the addition of the roof deck, the building still fits in with the
  overall mass and scale of surrounding development.

  The project site is located on the east side of Claressa Avenue between Beacon Street and
  Tremont Street. This is a heavily traveled area and both streets are identified as Major
  Circulation Facilities in the General Plan Circulation Element. There have been no reported
  traffic issues associated with the residence, and it is anticipated that existing infrastructure
  will ensure that traffic associated with the residence will not interfere with circulation along
  Claressa Avenue.

  The project site is located in an area with access to all necessary utilities and services to
  support the proposed use, including electric, water, gas, sewer, saltwater, and internet.

3. Every use, development of land, application of development standards shall be
  considered on the basis of suitable and functional development design, but is not
  intended that such approval be interpreted to require a particular style or type of
  architecture. (AMC Section 9-8.203.c)

  The project site is located within a developed area of Avalon, on an urbanized parcel
  surrounded by other residential buildings. The design elements in the proposed plans are
  consistent with the established scale of the buildings and structures within the community
  and will not stand out as inconsistent with existing development on the site or in the
  vicinity.

  5
 SECTION 3 – ADMINISTRATION AND CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL

  1. Based on the entire record before the Planning Commission and all written and oral
  evidence presented to the Planning Commission, the Planning Commission hereby finds
  the property Site is excluded from Coastal Development Permit requirements per Avalon
  Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-8.102.b.7.

  2. Based on the entire record before the Planning Commission, all written and oral evidence
  presented to the Planning Commission, and the findings set forth in this Resolution PC 25-
  07, the Planning Commission approves the Variance and Site Plan.

  3. The Chair of the Planning Commission shall sign this Resolution PC 25-07 and the
  Secretary of the Planning Commission shall certify the adoption thereof.

  BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a copy of this Resolution PC 25-07 be delivered to
the City Clerk of Avalon and a copy be sent to the Applicant at the address set forth in the
application for the Variance and Site Plan.

1. The project shall conform in substance and be maintained in general conformance with

2. Except as otherwise provided herein, this project is approved as a precise plan. After any

5. Pursuant to AMC Section 9-8.208, this approval for a Site Plan and Variance shall expire

   AVALON PLANNING COMMISSION
  STAFF REPORT – PC# 2882
  Wednesday, June 18, 2025

  Application File: CUP, Sign Variance
Item No.  4 – Public Hearing  Submitted by: Kaden Likins, Contract Planner

A Public Hearing considering a Conditional Use Permit and Sign Variance to allow an ice cream
shop (La Michoacana Premium) in the Commercial (C) zone at Metropole Market Place. The
Proposed Project is categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Existing Facilities). If denied, the Proposed Project is
statutorily exempt from CEQA per State CEQA Guidelines 15270 (Projects Which Are
Disapproved). The Proposed Project is located within the Coastal Zone and is excluded from
Coastal Development Permit requirements per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-
8.102.b.2.

  Applicant:  Alfonso Romero – La Michoacana Premium
  Owner:  Yolando Say -– Metropole Market Place, LLC
  Files:  CUP, Sign Variance
  Location of Project: 205 Crescent Avenue, Suite 105
  APN:  7480-018-001
  PC #:  2882
  File Date:  5/20/2025
  General Plan:  Commercial (C)
  Zone:  Commercial (C)

  BACKGROUND

Existing Site:

The project site is located within a large, irregularly shaped parcel approximately 10,739 square
feet in size. Known as Metropole Market Place, the site is currently developed with multiple
commercial businesses, including the Catalina Kids clothing store, Afishinados Gallery, CSC
Boardshop, and more antique retail stores. The center is also developed with restaurants like Coney

  2
 Island West, Café Metropole and M Restaurants & Events. Additional uses consist of the Three
Palms Avalon Arcade, Catalina Tours, and Hotel Metropole. La Michoacana Premium is to take
the place of CSC Boardshop, located in Suite 105 on the northeastern boundary of the Metropole
Market Place along Crescent Avenue.

Existing Area Context:

The project site is located on Crescent Avenue, between Whittley Avenue and Metropole Avenue.
This area is located in the heart of the downtown commercial district and consists of a mix of
commercial and public uses serving visitors and residents. Surrounding uses include hotels,
restaurants, retail, short-term rentals, and limited single family residential.

Entitlement and Permit History:

On March 21, 2023, the Planning Commission approved a Conditional Use Permit (PC#2834, PC
Resolution No. 23-07) for a General Retail store, CSC Boardshop, to operate the same location as
the current application. CSC Boardshop has operated in the suite since that time and La
Michoacana proposes to take over the entire suite.

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The applicant, La Michoacana Premium, leases an approximately 1,282 square foot unit within the
Metropole Market Place. La Michoacana Premium is taking the place of the previous tenant, CSC
Boardshop, who used the space for retail. The proposed use falls within the category of “restaurant,
bar, café”, which requires a Conditional Use Permit per AMC Section 9-6.203.a.3. The proposed
project consists of tenant improvement to update the floor plan to include an 80 square foot walk
in cooler and a 426 square foot storage area in the rear divided by a new non-load-bearing wall
with a 523 square foot service area on the other side. The service area includes a new preparation
sink, hand sink and a 3-compartment sink as well as refrigeration and additional counter space and
small equipment. There will also be new electrical wiring for all equipment as well as the
installation of floor and wall drains for dipper walls and a mop sink. The proposed operations
consist of the following:

  •  To offer a premium selection of ice cream flavors and diverse options of sweet treats,
  including ice cream, handcrafted popsicles, chocolate paletas, crepes, mini pancakes, fruit
  cups, chips, aguas fresca, and veggie juices, aiming to be a one-stop shop for sweet and
  savory cravings.

  •  Staffing will consist of 1 to 4 employees per shift. Each shift is to be scheduled according
  to the operational mode and dependent on the shop’s needs.

  •  Restrooms are provided via the nearby public restroom located in the Metropole Market
  Place.

  3
   •  Hours of operation from 8:00AM to 10:00PM daily in the spring and summer during the
  more visitor-heavy season and hours will vary depending on demand in the fall and winter
  during the less visitor-heavy season.

  •  Access to the unit is provided from the Crescent Avenue, consisting of pedestrian access
  with a designated sidewalk. There are also three temporary parking spaces located directly
  in front of the unit.

  •  Signage will consist of two signs that total 20 square feet. The larger of the two signs will
  be located above the entrance doors and will total 14 square feet. The sign will be
  maroon/purple and is 1 foot and 9 inches tall and 8 feet in length. The larger sign will
  encroach into the public right of way. The second sign totals 6 square feet and is located
  on the northern corner of the building. The sign is a round illuminated blade sign that totals
  6 square feet at 36 inches in height and width. The sign hangs 14 inches away from the
  building as a blade sign and has an ice cream cone and a popsicle with the business name,
  all illuminated on a black background. The applicant is requesting a sign variance for two
  signs that total 20 square feet in size, establishing non-conformance with AMC Section 9-
  7.709.j.

  o If signage is approved, the applicant will be required to obtain an encroachment
  permit for the both signs that encroach over the public right of way.

  DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

Issue #1: Variance for Sign:

The applicant is requesting a variance to allow a total of 20 square feet of signage for a commercial
tenant space in the Metropole Maret Place. The proposal includes the following:

  •  14 square foot entrance sign overhanging the entrance doors
  •  6 square foot round blade sign on the northern corner of the building

Pursuant to AMC Section 9-7.709.j, signs in the Commercial and Special Commercial zones shall
not exceed an area of eight feet per sign face. For businesses adjacent to two public right-of-way’s,
a total of two sign faces exceeding 16 square feet in combined area shall not be permitted.

Approval of the variance would grant special privileges to the applicant not afforded to other
businesses in similar circumstances. The tenant suite, suite 105, is located along a well-traveled
public walkway and transit area, providing plenty of visibility under existing sign requirements.
Adjacent nearby businesses have implemented compliant and effective signage visible from the
public right-of-way without the need for a variance. The previous tenant in Suite 105 also
maintained signage in conformance with AMC standards while remaining clearly visible to the
walkways and transit areas.

  4
 Additionally, suite 105 contains expansive street-facing windows that provide the applicant
opportunity to implement interior window signage, further enhancing signage without the need for
a variance.

renting or leasing of a room or rooms for periods of fewer than thirty (30) consecutive days

(CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15305 (Minor Alterations to Land Use Limitations) and

  AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES

Grandfathered Short-term Rentals are defined as properties renting for a period of 30 days or
less which have maintained a continuous business license history prior to 1988 through Fiscal Year
2024 (FY2024). These properties are nonconforming uses under the provisions of the AMC, as
they do not have a valid CUP or TRL authorizing their operation.

Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-8.702.b.1. states the following:

  “Discontinuance of a nonconforming use as indicated herein shall immediately terminate
  the right to operate such nonconforming use, except when extended as otherwise provided
  in this title.”

  DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

All property owners returned a completed Challenge Form by the June 9, 2025, deadline.

A summary of the facts related to each property, including use status, last year of active business
license, last month TOT payments were remitted, year of last property sale, and reason for the
challenge are included as Attachment 1. All returned forms are provided as Attachment 2 of this
report.

It is the determination of the City that failure to maintain a current City business license and/or
report or remit TOT for more than a year suggests that the subject properties have not been used
for the purpose of a short-term rental for more than a year. Therefore, properties that have not been
used as a short-term rental are not in compliance with the operational requirements for a
Grandfathered Short-term Rental, and all non-operational properties should have their ability to
operate as a nonconforming short-term rental terminated based on the terms set for in AMC Section
9-8.702.b. There is no process available in the AMC to allow property owners to “cure” the failure
to use a property for an established nonconforming use.

It has been an internal policy of the City to allow Grandfathered Short-term Rentals to retain, or
“bank”, the ability to short-term rent a property in the future, consistent with the process provided
to short-term rental Conditional Use Permits and Transient Rental Licenses, so long as a year-
round rental is documented. AMC Section 9-8.411 provides that conditional use permits or other
legally nonconforming uses shall not terminate if the use is suspended for one year while a unit is
being rented on an annual term, as long as notice was provided to the Planning Department, along
with evidence of such lease. The purpose of this rule is to encourage long-term rental in the City
to increase housing opportunities for residents and the City’s workforce. Therefore, consideration

  2
 has been given to properties which currently maintain a business license and active lease for year-
round rental.

Based on the licensing history of the property and information provided by the property owners,
staff makes the following recommendations for each challenge list property:

Individual resolutions, reflective of staff’s recommended action and associated findings, are
included as Attachments 3 through 10 of this staff report.

All properties recommended for revocation have not maintained a current City business license
and/or have failed to report or remit TOT for more than a year. Many of the property owners
indicated in their challenge forms that they were unaware of the nonconforming status of their
properties. But AMC Section 9-8.702.b.1 does not contain a carve out for those who do not use
their legally nonconforming use for lack of knowledge of it. Generally, the purpose of legal
nonconforming regulations is to prevent the sudden loss in the value of an investment due to a
change in law. Relatedly, there is a general preference to encourage the eventual elimination of
nonconforming uses. One appropriate circumstance to terminate a nonconforming use is when the
use has been discontinued, where a lack of knowledge of the nonconforming use indicates that
there was no expectation on part of the property owner that the use would continue.

One property, 360 Clemente Avenue A2, has retained a year-round rental business license in good
standing and has an active lease on file with the Finance Department. Therefore, this property is
recommended to be allowed to retain their Grandfathered Short-term Rental status by virtue of
substantial compliance with AMC Section 9-8.411.

Should properties with revoked Grandfathered Short-term Rental status wish to operate as a
transient rental in the future, they may apply for a Transient Rental License consistent with current
City regulations.

   ENVIRONMENTAL DETERMINATION

The proposed project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental
Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15305 (Class 5 – Minor Alterations to Land Use
Limitations) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the environment. The Class 5
exemption consists of minor alterations in land use limitations in areas with an average slope of
less than 20%, which do not result in any changes in land use or density.

In addition, the project is categorically exempt from the provisions of CEQA per State CEQA
Guidelines 15321 (Class 21 – Enforcement Actions by Regulatory Agencies). The Class 21
exemption includes actions by regulatory agencies to enforce or revoke a lease, permit, license,
certificate, or other entitlement for use issued, adopted, or prescribed by the regulatory agency or
enforcement of a law, general rule, standard, or objective, administered or adopted by the
regulatory agency.

The project consists of revocation of licenses and entitlements for a property that is not in
compliance with the operational regulations for a Conditional Use Permit or Transient Rental for
transient occupancy rental of an existing dwelling unit. As such, the project is not expected to have
a detrimental impact on the environment of the various property locations or surrounding area.

Further, none of the exceptions to the use of categorical exemptions stated in State CEQA
Guidelines section 15300.2 apply: The project is not located in a particularly sensitive environment
because it is proposed in an area already developed for residential uses. No cumulative impact
would occur from this project’s approval, there will be no significant effect on the environment
because the Project, and no damage to scenic resources will occur because this project, because
the project consists of licensing of an existing developed property, with no new or expanded
development proposed. The project is not located on a hazardous waste site, and the project does
not involve substantial impacts to a historical resource.

   RESOLUTION NO. PC 25-17

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  AVALON TERMINATING THE NONCONFORMING STATUS OF A
  GRANDFATHERED SHORT-TERM RENTAL PROPERTY TO
  CONDUCT TRANSIENT OCCUPANCY RENTAL AT 8 CAMINO DE
  FLORES (PC#2879)

  WHEREAS, pursuant to California Constitution Article XI, § 7, State of California Zoning
and Planning Law (Government Code section 65800-65912) and Chapter 9-8 of the Avalon
Municipal Code ("AMC"), the City of Avalon Planning Commission ("Planning Commission")
is authorized to make a determination regarding the status of and termination of the nonconforming
use of the property located at 8 Camino de Flores (APN 7480-049-061) (“Property”); and

  WHEREAS, a “Grandfathered Short-term Rental” is defined as a property rented for a
period of 30 days or less which have maintained a continuous business license history prior to
1988 through Fiscal Year 2024 (FY2024); and.

  WHEREAS, Grandfathered Short-term Rentals are nonconforming uses under the
provisions of Article 7 of Chapter 9-8 of the AMC, as they do not have a valid Conditional Use
Permit or Transient Rental License authorizing their operation; and

  WHEREAS, an application was initiated by the City of Avalon to terminate the continued
use of the subject Property as a Grandfathered Short-term Rental (“Project”); and

  WHEREAS, AMC Section 9-8.702.b.1 states that the discontinuance of a nonconforming
use shall immediately terminate the right to operate such nonconforming use, except when
extended as otherwise provided in Title 9, Planning and Zoning; and

  WHEREAS, the subject Property has failed to maintain a current City business license or
remit transient occupancy tax for transient occupancy rental for more than one year, and has not
applied for a business license in FY2024; and

  WHEREAS, the owners of the Property, Lincoln and Marina Bandlow (“Owner”), were
properly notified of public hearings held on May 21, 2025, and June 18, 2025, to determine
whether the Planning Commission should terminate the nonconforming status of the Property as a
Grandfathered Short-term Rental; and

  WHEREAS, on May 21, 2025, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public
hearing, at which time interested parties were afforded the opportunity to testify either in support
of or opposition to the termination of the nonconforming status of the Property as a Grandfathered
Short-term Rental; and

  WHEREAS, on May 21, 2025, the Planning Commission voted to continue the public
hearing for properties which challenged the termination of their Grandfathered Short-term Rental
status to a date certain for further consideration, including the subject Property;
  1
   WHEREAS, on June 18, 2025, the Planning Commission continued the duly noticed
public hearing, at which time interested parties were afforded the opportunity to testify either in
support of or opposition to the termination of the nonconforming status of the Property as a
Grandfathered Short-term Rental; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission carefully considered all information pertaining to
the Project, including the licensing history of the Property, the transient rental revocation challenge
form submitted by the Owner, and testimony presented at its public hearings on May 21, 2025,
and June 18, 2025; and

  WHEREAS, the Project was found to be categorically exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15305 (Minor Alterations to Land
Use Limitations) and 15321 (Enforcement Actions by Regulatory Agencies); and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Resolution have
occurred.

  NOW THEREFORE, THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
AVALON DOES HEREBY RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The recitals set forth above are true and correct and are incorporated herein
by reference.

  SECTION 2. Based on the preponderance of the evidence presented to this Commission
at the above-referenced public hearings on May 21, 2025, and June 18, 2025, including the
staff reports and all related information presented to the Planning Commission, the following
findings are made in accordance with Section 9-8.702.b.1 of the Avalon Municipal Code.

  1. The Property has been identified through City records as a Grandfathered Short-term
  Rental, which has in the past operated as transient occupancy rental with a City business
  license.

  2. The subject Property has not been issued a Conditional Use Permit under AMC Article 1
  of Chapter 9-8 of Title 9 or a Transient Rental License under AMC Article 3 of Chapter
  3-1 of Title 3 for transient occupancy rental.

  3. AMC Section 9-8.702.b.1 states that “Discontinuance of a nonconforming use as
  indicated herein shall immediately terminate the right to operate such nonconforming use,
  except when extended as otherwise provided in this title.”

  4. A review of the City's records confirms that the Property has not maintained a transient
  occupancy rental business license, nor has any income or tax been reported or remitted
  for FY2024 or more than one year. 2022 is the last year a City short-term rental business
  license was associated with the property, and TOT was last remitted to the Finance
  Department in November 2020.

  5. Since a business license must be annually renewed per AMC 3-1.123 and is required by

  2
   AMC Section 3-1.103, and reporting and remitting TOT is required by AMC Section 3-
  3.407, failing to do so indicates that the use of the Grandfathered Short-term Rental has
  been discontinued the Property.

  6. Based on the foregoing, the Planning Commission hereby finds that the Property has not
  been used for transient occupancy use for more than a year, justifying the termination of
  the nonconforming status of the Property under AMC Section 9-8.702.b as a
  Grandfathered Short-term Rental.

Based upon these findings, the Planning Commission hereby terminates the nonconforming status
allowing transient occupancy rental of the subject Property as a Grandfathered Short-term Rental.

  SECTION 3. The Project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15305 (Class 5 – Minor
Alterations to Land Use Limitations) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment. The Class 5 exemption consists of minor alterations in land use limitations in areas
with an average slope of less than 20%, which do not result in any changes in land use or density.

In addition, the Project is categorically exempt from the provisions of CEQA per State CEQA
Guidelines 15321 (Class 21 – Enforcement Actions by Regulatory Agencies). The Class 21
exemption includes actions by regulatory agencies to enforce or revoke a lease, permit, license,
certificate, or other entitlement for use issued, adopted, or prescribed by the regulatory agency or
enforcement of a law, general rule, standard, or objective, administered or adopted by the
regulatory agency.

The Project consists of revocation of licenses and entitlements for a property that is not in
compliance with the operational regulations for a Conditional Use Permit or Transient Rental for
transient occupancy rental of an existing dwelling unit. As such, the project is not expected to have
a detrimental impact on the environment of the various property locations or surrounding area.

Further, none of the exceptions to the use of categorical exemptions stated in State CEQA
Guidelines section 15300.2 apply: The Project is not located in a particularly sensitive environment
because it is proposed in an area already developed for residential uses. No cumulative impact
would occur from the Project’s approval, there will be no significant effect on the environment
because the Project, and no damage to scenic resources will occur because this Project, because
the Project consists of licensing of an existing developed property, with no new or expanded
development proposed. The Project is not located on a hazardous waste site, and the project does
not involve substantial impacts to a historical resource.

  SECTION 4. This action by the Planning Commission shall be final unless appeal of
the action is filed with the City Clerk's office in writing, pursuant to Section 9-8.601 of the AMC.

  SECTION 5.  Severability. If any section, subsection, sentence, clause, phrase or word
of this Resolution is found to be unconstitutional or otherwise invalid by any court of competent
jurisdiction, such decision shall not affect the remaining provisions of this Resolution.

  3

the City of Avalon City Clerk for transmittal to the City of Avalon City Council.

  AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES

Conditional Use Permits are defined as properties renting for a period of 30 days or less with
approval of a CUP granted by the Planning Commission between 1988 and 2020.

AMC Section 9-8.501.a-c authorizes the Planning Commission to revoke or modify a Conditional
Use Permit based on the following grounds:

  (a) That such variance, conditional use permit or nonconforming use was obtained by
  fraud; or
  (b) That such variance, conditional use permit or nonconforming use was not being
  exercised; or
  (c) That such variance, conditional use permit or nonconforming use has ceased or has
  been suspended for one year or more.

Transient Rental License are defined as properties renting for a period of 30 days or less with
approval of a TRL granted by the Planning Commission between 2021 to the present.

AMC Section 3-1.312.a authorizes the Planning Commission revoke a Transient Rental Licenses
pursuant to the following:

  “(a) Any Transient Rental License issued under this article may be revoked or suspended
  where:

  (1) The licensee has violated any provision of this article;
  (2) Where a license has been granted on false or fraudulent evidence, testimony or
  application; or
  (3) Where the licensee has violated the terms and conditions of the license, including,
  but not limited to, the timely payment of fees required by this article.”

Grandfathered Short-term Rentals are defined as properties renting for a period of 30 days or
less which have maintained a continuous business license history prior to 1988 through Fiscal Year
(FY) 2024. These properties are nonconforming uses under the provisions of the AMC, as they do
not have a valid CUP or TRL authorizing their operation.

Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-8.702.b.1. states the following regarding the termination
of nonconforming uses:

  “Discontinuance of a nonconforming use as indicated herein shall immediately terminate
  the right to operate such nonconforming use, except when extended as otherwise provided
  in this title.”

   DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

All property owners returned a completed Challenge Form prior to publication of the meeting
agenda.

A summary of the facts related to each property, including use status, last year of active business
license, last month TOT payments were remitted, year of last property sale, and reason for the
challenge are included as Attachment 1. All returned forms are provided as Attachment 2 of this
report.

Payment of Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT)
Failure to report transient rental income for more than a year evidences that the subject properties
have not been used for the purpose of a short-term rental for more than a year. If used for transient
occupancy purposes, the operator of the property is required to collect TOT and remit it to the
City. This tax applies to all transient rentals. If no tax is paid, the owner of the unit evidences that
the property is not used for vacation rental. And if the tax is collected and not remitted to the
City, the operator is pocketing the tax collected, enriching itself at the expense of the City. This
is also grounds for revocation.

Annual/Year-round Residential Rentals
AMC Section 9-8.411 provides that conditional use permits or other legally nonconforming uses
shall not terminate if the use is suspended for one year while a unit is being rented on an annual
term, as long as notice was provided to the Planning Department, along with evidence of such
lease. The purpose of this rule is to encourage long-term rental in the City to increase housing
opportunities for residents and the City’s workforce. Therefore, whether to revoke entitlements as
to properties which currently maintain a business license and active lease for year-round rental has
been considered in light of the intent of AMC Section 9-8.411.

  TERM RENTAL PROPERTY CONDUCTING TRANSIENT OCCUPANCY
  RENTAL AT 5 CAMINO DE FLORES (PC#2880)

  WHEREAS, pursuant to California Constitution Article XI, § 7, State of California Zoning
and Planning Law (Government Code section 65800-65912) and Chapter 9-8 of the Avalon
Municipal Code ("AMC"), the City of Avalon Planning Commission ("Planning Commission")
is authorized to make a determination regarding the status of the nonconforming use at the property
located at 5 Camino de Flores (APN 7480-0490062) (“Property”); and

  WHEREAS, a “Grandfathered Short-term Rental” is defined as a property rented for a
period of 30 days or less which have maintained a continuous business license history prior to
1988 through Fiscal Year 2024 (FY2024); and

  WHEREAS, Grandfathered Short-term Rentals are nonconforming uses under the
provisions of the AMC, as they do not have a valid Conditional Use Permit or Transient Rental
License authorizing their operation; and

  WHEREAS, an application was initiated by the City of Avalon to terminate the continued
use of the subject Property as Grandfathered Short-term Rental (“Project”); and

  WHEREAS, AMC Section 9-8.702.b.1 states that the discontinuance of a nonconforming
use shall immediately terminate the right to operate such nonconforming use, except when
extended as otherwise provided in Title 9, Planning and Zoning; and

  WHEREAS, the subject Property has a current City business license for transient
occupancy rental, but had not reported or remitted any transient occupancy tax (TOT) payments
to the City since the beginning of FY2024 or before; and

  WHEREAS, the owner of record of the Property, Maurice Loomis (“Owner”), was
properly notified of the public hearings held on May 21, 2025, and June 18, 2025, to determine
whether the Planning Commission should terminate the nonconforming status of the Property as
Grandfathered Short-term Rental; and

  WHEREAS, on May 21, 2025, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public
hearing, at which time interested parties were afforded the opportunity to testify either in support
of or opposition to the termination of the nonconforming status of the Property as a Grandfathered
Short-term Rental; and

  WHEREAS, on May 21, 2025, the Planning Commission voted to continue the public
hearing for properties which challenged the termination of their Grandfathered Short-term Rental
status to a date certain for further consideration, including the subject Property; and

  1
   WHEREAS, on June 18, 2025, the Planning Commission continued the duly noticed
public hearing, at which time interested parties were afforded the opportunity to testify either in
support of or opposition to the termination of the nonconforming status of the Property as a
Grandfathered Short-term Rental; and

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission carefully considered all information pertaining to
the Project, including the licensing history of the Property, the transient rental revocation challenge
form submitted by the Owner, and testimony presented at its public hearings on May 21, 2025,
and June 18, 2025; and

  WHEREAS, the Project was found to be categorically exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15305 (Minor Alterations to Land
Use Limitations) and 15321 (Enforcement Actions by Regulatory Agencies); and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Resolution have
occurred.

  NOW THEREFORE, THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
AVALON DOES HEREBY RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The recitals set forth above are true and correct and are incorporated herein
by reference.

  SECTION 2. Based on the preponderance of the evidence presented to this Commission
at the above-referenced public hearings on May 21, 2025, and June 18, 2025, including the
staff report and all related information presented to the Planning Commission, the following
findings are made in accordance with Section 9-8.702.b.1 of the Avalon Municipal Code.

  1. The Property has been identified through City records as Grandfathered Short-term
  Rental, which has in the past operated transient occupancy rental with a City business
  license.

  2. The subject Property has not been issued a Conditional Use Permit or Transient Rental
  License under the Avalon Municipal Code for transient occupancy rental.

  3. AMC Section 9-8.702.b.1 states that “Discontinuance of a nonconforming use as
  indicated herein shall immediately terminate the right to operate such nonconforming use,
  except when extended as otherwise provided in this title.”

  4. All those engaging in transient rental in the City must remit TOT to the City. (AMC
  Section 3-3.407) Those collecting TOT must also engage in reporting of all transient
  rental activities on the form provided by the Finance Director. (AMC Section 3-3.407)

  5. A review of the City's records confirms that the Property has maintained a transient
  occupancy rental business license, and as of the adoption of this resolution all transient

  2
   occupancy tax (TOT) has been reported or remitted to the Finance Department since
  FY2024 or before in accordance with Article 4 of Chapter 3-3 of Title 3 of the Avalon
  Municipal Code.

  6. Since the Property has reported or remitted TOT to the City, this evidences that the
  transient rental use has not been discontinued as provided in AMC Section 9-8.702.b.1.

  of the Property for transient rental has not been discontinued for at least a one year period,
  justifying the continuance of the nonconforming status of the Property under AMC
  Section 9-8.702.b as a Grandfathered Short-term Rental.

Based upon these findings, the Planning Commission hereby affirms the continued nonconforming
status allowing transient occupancy rental of the subject Property as a Grandfathered Short-term
Rental.

Alterations to Land Use Limitations) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment. The Class 5 exemption consists of minor alterations in land use limitations in areas
with an average slope of less than 20%, which do not result in any changes in land use or density.

In additional, the Project is categorically exempt from the provisions of CEQA per State CEQA

  AUTHORIZING GUIDELINES

Conditional Use Permits are defined as properties renting for a period of 30 days or less with
approval of a CUP granted by the Planning Commission between 1988 and 2020.

AMC Section 9-8.501.a-c authorizes the Planning Commission to revoke or modify a Conditional
Use Permit based on the following grounds:

  (a) That such variance, conditional use permit or nonconforming use was obtained by
  fraud; or
  (b) That such variance, conditional use permit or nonconforming use was not being
  exercised; or
  (c) That such variance, conditional use permit or nonconforming use has ceased or has
  been suspended for one year or more.

Transient Rental License are defined as properties renting for a period of 30 days or less with
approval of a TRL granted by the Planning Commission between 2021 to the present.

  2
 AMC Section 3-1.312.a authorizes the Planning Commission revoke a Transient Rental Licenses
pursuant to the following:

  “(a) Any Transient Rental License issued under this article may be revoked or suspended
  where:

  (1) The licensee has violated any provision of this article;
  (2) Where a license has been granted on false or fraudulent evidence, testimony or
  application; or
  (3) Where the licensee has violated the terms and conditions of the license, including,
  but not limited to, the timely payment of fees required by this article.”

  DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

All property owners returned a completed Challenge Form prior to publication of the meeting
agenda.

A summary of the facts related to each property, including use status, last year of active business
license, last month TOT payments were remitted, year of last property sale, and reason for the
challenge are included as Attachment 1. All returned forms are provided as Attachment 2 of this
report.

It is the determination of the City that failure to maintain a current City business license and/or
report or remit TOT for more than a year suggests that the subject properties have not been used
for the purpose of a short-term rental for more than a year. Therefore, properties that have not been
used as a short-term rental are not in compliance with the operational requirements for a
Conditional Use Permit or Transient Rental License, and all non-operational properties should
have their ability to operate as a nonconforming short-term rental terminated based on the terms
set for in AMC Section 9-8.501a-c or 3-1.312.a. There is no process available in the AMC to allow
property owners to “cure” the failure to use a property when the property is not operating consistent
with a previously approved use.

AMC Section 9-8.411 provides that conditional use permits or other legally nonconforming uses
shall not terminate if the use is suspended for one year while a unit is being rented on an annual
term, as long as notice was provided to the Planning Department, along with evidence of such
lease. The purpose of this rule is to encourage long-term rental in the City to increase housing
opportunities for residents and the City’s workforce. Therefore, whether to revoke entitlements to
properties which currently maintain a business license and active lease for year-round rental has
been considered in light of AMC Section 9-8.411.

   RESOLUTION NO. PC 25-30

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
  AVALON REVOKING THE CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT ALLOWING
  TRANSIENT OCCUPANCY RENTAL AT 18 CANYON TERRACE
  (PC#2881)

  WHEREAS, pursuant to California Constitution Article XI, § 7, State of California Zoning
and Planning Law (Government Code section 65800-65912) and Chapter 9-8 of the Avalon
Municipal Code ("AMC"), the City of Avalon Planning Commission ("Planning Commission")
is authorized to revoke the conditional use permit allowing transient occupancy rental at the
property located at 18 Canyon Terrace (APN 7480-008-035) (“Property”); and

  WHEREAS, an application was initiated by the City of Avalon to revoke the conditional
use permit for the subject Property (“Project”); and

  WHEREAS, AMC section 9-8.501.b authorizes the Planning Commission to move to
revoke a conditional use permit upon a finding that the conditional use permit is not being
exercised; and

  WHEREAS, AMC section 9-8.501.c authorizes the Planning Commission to move to
revoke a conditional use permit upon a finding that the conditional use permit has been suspended
for one year or more; and

  WHEREAS, the subject Property has not maintained a current City business license for
transient occupancy rental, and have not reported or remitted any transient occupancy tax (TOT)
payments to the City since the beginning of Fiscal Year 2024 (FY2024) or before; and

  WHEREAS, the owner of record of the property, EUBANK ERIN M TR (“Owner”), was
properly notified of a public hearing held on May 21, 2025, and June 18, 2025, to determine
whether the Planning Commission should revoke the conditional use permit approval for transient
occupancy rental; and

  WHEREAS, on May 21, 2025, the Planning Commission conducted a duly noticed public
hearing, at which time interested parties were afforded the opportunity to testify either in support
of or opposition to the termination of the conditional use permit for transient occupancy of the
Property; and

  WHEREAS, on May 21, 2025, the Planning Commission voted to continue the public
hearing for properties which challenged the termination of their conditional use permits or transient
rental licenses to a date certain for further consideration, including the subject Property; and

  WHEREAS, on June 18, 2025, the Planning Commission continued the duly noticed
public hearing, at which time interested parties were afforded the opportunity to testify either in
support of or opposition to the termination of the conditional use permit for transient occupancy
of the Property; and

  1
   WHEREAS, the Planning Commission carefully considered all information pertaining to
the Project, including the licensing history of the Property, the transient rental revocation challenge
form submitted by the Owner, and testimony presented at its public hearings on May 21, 2025,
and June 18, 2025; and

  WHEREAS, the Project was found to be categorically exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15305 (Minor Alterations to Land
Use Limitations) and 15321 (Enforcement Actions by Regulatory Agencies); and

  WHEREAS, all other legal prerequisites to the adoption of this Resolution have
occurred.

  NOW THEREFORE, THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
AVALON DOES HEREBY RESOLVE AS FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The recitals set forth above are true and correct and are incorporated herein
by reference.

  SECTION 2. Based on the preponderance of the evidence presented to this Commission
at the above-referenced public hearings on May 21, 2025, and June 18, 2025, including the
staff report and all related information presented to the Planning Commission, the following
findings are made in accordance with Chapter 9-8 of the Avalon Municipal Code.

  1. The subject Property holds a conditional use permit for transient rental occupancy,
  approved by the Planning Commission in 2020 (PC#2358).

  2. AMC Section 3-1.103 requires that no person shall commence, or carry on, either directly
  or indirectly, any business without first having obtained and maintained in good standing
  a business license.

  3. Article 4 of Chapter 3-3 of Title 3 of the AMC requires that all transient rentals shall be
  subject to collection of transient occupancy tax (TOT).

  4. AMC Section 3-3.407 requires that all income earned from transient occupancy rentals
  be reported to the City, and that the appropriate amount of tax also be remitted to the City.

  5. A review of the City's records confirms that the Property has not maintained a transient
  occupancy rental business license, and no income or transient occupancy tax (TOT) has
  been reported or remitted to the Finance Department since FY2024 or before. No recent
  business license history was found for the property, and no TOT payments have been
  remitted to the City in the last seven years.

  6. Since maintaining a business license is a requirement to operate a conditional use permit,
  the failure to maintain a license indicates that no transient rental is occurring on the
  Property. Similarly, payment and reporting of TOT is a requirement of conducting
  transient rental in the City, and a failure to pay TOT evidences that no transient rental is
  occurring on the subject Property.

  2
   7. AMC Section 9-8.501.b provides that a conditional use permit may be revoked if it is not
  being exercised. Avalon Municipal Code section 9-8.501.c provides that a conditional use
  permit may be revoked following one year of non-use.

  8. Based on the foregoing, the Planning Commission hereby finds that the conditional use
  permit for the subject Property has not been used for transient occupancy use for more
  than a year, justifying the termination of the conditional use permit under AMC Sections
  9-8.501.b and 9-8.501.c.

Based upon these findings, the Planning Commission hereby revokes the conditional use permit
allowing transient occupancy rental of the subject Property.

  SECTION 3. The Project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15305 (Class 5 – Minor
Alterations to Land Use Limitations) because it has no potential to have a significant effect on the
environment. The Class 5 exemption consists of minor alterations in land use limitations in areas
with an average slope of less than 20%, which do not result in any changes in land use or density.

In additional, the Project is categorically exempt from the provisions of CEQA per State CEQA
Guidelines 15321 (Class 21 – Enforcement Actions by Regulatory Agencies). The Class 21
exemption includes actions by regulatory agencies to enforce or revoke a lease, permit license,
certificate, or other entitlement for use issued, adopted, or prescribed by the regulatory agency or
enforcement of a law, general rule, standard, or objective, administered or adopted by the
regulatory agency.

The Project consists of revocation of licenses and entitlements for a property that is not in
compliance with the operational regulations for a Conditional Use Permit or Transient Rental for
transient occupancy rental of an existing dwelling unit. As such, the project is not expected to have
a detrimental impact on the environment of the various property locations or surrounding area.

  Wednesday, June 18, 2025

  Application File: N/A
Item No. 8  Submitted by: Kelly Ribuffo, Contract Planner

Consideration of a recommendation to the City Council regarding potential
modifications to the notice provisions for Transient Rental License public hearings as
provided in Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-1.109.b, Notice.

  BACKGROUND

On December 15, 2020 (effective February 1, 2021), the City Council adopted Ordinance No.
1922-20, which amended the Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) to remove all regulations related to
the short-term rental CUP from Title 9, Planning and Zoning, and adopted the current Transient
Rental License regulations as part of Title 3, Finance. All Transient Rental Licenses require
approval by the Planning Commission.

Prior to the adoption of the ordinance, the Planning Commission successfully requested staff
(1) amend the draft transient rental ordinance to clarify that a public hearing is necessary prior
to the issuance of a license (2) make notice provisions the same as public hearings for
consideration of transient rental CUP applications, and (3) codify language stating that the
Planning Commission will re-consider these notice requirements two years after the effective
date of the new ordinance.

AMC Section 3-1.109 sets forth requirements for license hearings, including application,
noticing, and license issuance procedures. Subsection (c) states that the Planning Commission
shall reconsider the notice provisions set for in Subsection (b) two years after adoption of
Article 3, Transient Rental Licenses. At the March 21, 2023, Special Joint City
Council/Planning Commission meeting, the notice provisions were reviewed and no
modifications were made at that time.

The existing Transient Rental License moratorium established by City Council through adoption
of Urgency Ordinance No. 1212-23 is set to expire on July 31, 2025. As part of the ongoing
discussion of potential modifications to transient rental regulations, staff requests that the Planning
Commission review the notice provisions again and provide recommendations to City Council as

   EXISTING NOTICE PROVISIONS

AMC Section 3-1.109.b states:

“(b) Notice. Not less than 10 days prior to the date of a hearing on an application for a Transient
Rental License, the Planning Commission shall give notice which shall include the time, place,
and purpose of such hearing, the location of the property under consideration, and such other
information as it deems necessary as provided herein:

  (1) Cause a copy of such notice to be published once in a newspaper of general circulation
  in the City of Avalon;

  (2) Cause such notice to be mailed by first-class mail, postage prepaid, to the applicant and
  to all persons whose names and addresses appear on the latest available assessment roll of
  the County of Los Angeles as owning property within a distance of 300 feet from the
  exterior boundaries of the area for which an application for a Transient Rental License is
  filed, and to such other persons whose property or interests might, in the judgment of the
  Planning Commission or its designee, be affected by the issuance of the Transient Rental
  License requested. The Planning Commission shall also cause to be posted on the subject
  property in a location clearly visible from the street, a notice which measures at least 11
  inches by 14 inches and which contains the information included in the notice as set forth
  in paragraph (1) of this subsection; and

  (3) If the Planning Commission finds that the mailing of notices prescribed elsewhere in
  this section may not give sufficient notice to said persons, then such notices shall be posted
  at such locations as are deemed best suited to reach the attention of and inform those
  persons who may be affected.

  (4) Such notice shall be in addition to any notice required for the issuance of a Local
  Coastal Permit.”

AMC Section 3-1.109.c states:

  “(c) Reconsideration of Notice Provisions. The Planning Commission shall reconsider the
  notice provisions set forth in subsection (b) of this section two years after the adoption of
  this article.”
  DISCUSSION/ RECOMMENDATION

The existing notice provisions meet the minimum requirements for a public hearing under
State law, pursuant to Gov Code §65091, and 65092. However, State law does not prevent a
jurisdiction from specifying additional duration or expanded methods of notice for projects

  2
 where it is deemed necessary reach the attention of and inform those persons who may be
affected by the action.

  Based on the facts noted in this staff report and documentation submitted by the Avalon
Planning Department, staff recommends that the Planning Commission continue with existing
notice requirements.
